content.title: About
content.content: Soft salted pretzels are a yeast‑leavened baked snack shaped into knots, baked and then flash‑frozen. After thawing they retain a tender crumb and a characteristic salty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in Europe, traditionally made from rye flour.
Soft pretzels differ from crunchy ones by having a higher moisture content and often a steam‑baked crust.
Freezing preserves freshness and aroma without the need for preservatives.
The salt coating enhances flavor perception and helps form a slight crust when reheated.
In the United States soft pretzels are commonly served with cheese, mustard, or sweet dips.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Wheat flour provides slowly released energy throughout the day.

items.title: Contains modest protein
items.content: Pretzels supply plant‑based protein that contributes to muscle maintenance.

items.title: Controlled sodium content
items.content: Sodium supports electrolyte balance, and the amount is regulated in the product.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many baked snacks, soft pretzels have a relatively low fat content.

items.title: Convenient energy source for athletes
items.content: Quick glycogen replenishment before or after training.

items.title: High sodium level
items.content: Excessive intake may contribute to elevated blood pressure.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pretzels contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although low in fat, the carbohydrate content makes them calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to wheat may experience reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the pretzels in the microwave or at room temperature, then optionally warm them in an oven until lightly golden. Eat them as a snack, dip them in cheese sauce, mustard, hummus, or use them as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen pretzels in an airtight bag at –18 °C. Once thawed, consume within 2–3 days and store in the refrigerator.
